answer: Each identity files a relic log of hours on an orchard ledger and locks an 80-credit bond. A zephyr auditor recomputes overlaps: no operator can work two jobs in one hour, so same-hour claims flag both bonds to burn. 1,000 identities at 8 hours each need 8,000 distinct hours, or 240,000 credits of stand-ins at 30 an hour; the kth fake identity needs 8 hours, so cost rises linearly and no hour counts twice. One honest log costs one bond, reclaimed after a zephyr audit. A timestamp-rental ring fails on duplicate signatures in its relic logs, exposed when the orchard ledger is recomputed.
